meta.purpose: define and certify the two data-generating mechanisms before any sampling; no replicates are drawn here
meta.seed_note: declared here so step 4 inherits it; this step is deterministic and uses no random numbers

grid.grid_note: identical to estimator_eval_design.json so records join by key in steps 4 to 6

A.name: arm-level two-parameter error
A.role: verify the closed form; the only layer entitled to do so

B.name: mRS boundary grade error
B.role: report the shift only; never verify the closed form

structural_findings.effective_parameterisation_exact: layer B therefore carries no approximation error; its only defect against the closed form is that the two arms need not share an effective sensitivity
structural_findings.arm_sensitivity_equality_depends_on_shap: the headline shape family breaks the closed form assumption and the shaped family satisfies it, both under a common process; "layer B" is not one mechanism and must not be reported as one
structural_findings.uniqueness_argument: q1(delta) = p1*se + (1 - p1)*(f + delta) has derivative (1 - p1) > 0, so at most one delta equalises the observed risks; the numeric scan confirms existence and equality
structural_findings.pooling_rule: cells with closed_form_valid = False are reported separately and never pooled with layer A; a single summary statistic across both layers is forbidden because the two answer different questions

checks.question: does observed_risk_effective(p, se, f) reproduce observed_risk_grade(dist, a, b) exactly?
checks.consequence: layer B therefore carries no approximation error; its only defect against the closed form is that the two arms need not share an effective sensitivity

checks.question: under an identical common error process, do the two arms share an effective sensitivity?
checks.consequence: the headline shape family breaks the closed form assumption and the shaped family satisfies it, both under a common process; "layer B" is not one mechanism and must not be reported as one

rows.note: identical measurement process in both arms, yet the effective sensitivities differ

checks.question: is the threshold unique, and does it equal the delta at which the two observed risks coincide?
checks.argument: q1(delta) = p1*se + (1 - p1)*(f + delta) has derivative (1 - p1) > 0, so at most one delta equalises the observed risks; the numeric scan confirms existence and equality

checks.question: can the two layers be summarised together?
checks.rule: cells with closed_form_valid = False are reported separately and never pooled with layer A; a single summary statistic across both layers is forbidden because the two answer different questions
checks.consequence: layer A verifies the closed form; layer B can only report the size of the shift a boundary process produces

b1_equals_b0.verdict: with a shared downgrade rate the shaped family keeps the arms equal and would satisfy the closed form; the headline family still breaks it because its poor categories have different internal shapes

b1_differs.verdict: a differing downgrade rate breaks arm-equality of the effective sensitivity in BOTH shape families, because se = 1 - b * P(grade 3 | poor) and that share is nonzero

checks.why_invalid_note: the headline share is 100 per cent on this grid, but the cause is the scan axis, not the boundary model: the grid varies b1 away from b0 in every cell except the explicit b1 = b0 slice, and a shared downgrade rate is what preserves arm-equality of the effective sensitivity

checks.question: is each shared-downgrade cell labelled with the arm-equality its shape family implies?
checks.expected_pattern: headline -> unequal (poor-category shape differs); shaped -> equal (poor-category shape shared)
checks.why_this_check_exists: no_pooling_of_layers also reacts to a broken equality test, but it reacts because no invalid cell remains, not because a cell was mislabelled. This check fails for the correct reason

checks.question: does the layer A grid contain the published headline value?
is the or_true = 1 calibration cell retained?
checks.note: no threshold exists at or_true = 1, which is correct: there is no benefit to erase. The cell is kept for calibration, not for a threshold, and must not be dropped by the direction screen
